Self-service book scanning is available (free, walk-up, no reservation needed) at several UVA libraries. Here's where to find them:

*Print/book scanning stations*

• ScannX Book ScanCenter (flatbed book-edge, up to 11"x17", 600dpi, OCR) — main floor in Brown, 4th floor in Clemons (2 units), 5th floor in Shannon
• KIC BookEye Overhead Scanner (with "V" cradle for holding books at 120°/180° angle, up to 24"x18", 600dpi, OCR) — 4th floor in Clemons, main level in Music, 2nd/3rd/4th floors in Shannon
• Epson Expression 13000XL (flatbed, up to 12.2"x17.2", very high resolution up to 2400x4800dpi, OCR) — 1st floor in Fine Arts (3 units), 3rd floor in Shannon (Scholars' Lab, room 308)
• Fujitsu fi-8270 Color Duplex Document Scanner (100-page auto feeder, 8.5"x14") — Shannon Library

*Other related scanning*

• Microfilm scanners — Shannon Library, 1st floor, Government Documents room 130 (staff can assist)
• Non-print media (film, VHS, slides, etc.) — Robertson Media Center (RMC), 3rd floor of Clemons — these are not available for checkout, walk-up use only
• Fine Arts Library also has Apple computers on the 1st floor with Epson scanners + Photoshop for digitizing film negatives, slides, and documents

All of these are free self-service walk-up stations — staff at each library's info/service desk can help if needed. For more detail see: <https://www.library.virginia.edu/services/scanning-self-service|Self-service scanning & digitization | UVA Library>

If you need a portion of a book scanned for you (e.g., from closed stacks like Ivy Stacks), you can request that via Virgo's "Request a scan" option — see: <https://answers.lib.virginia.edu/faq/294551|How can I request scanning for a portion of a book?>
